label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
statement_en: In an isometric family an area scales as the square of the linear dimension, S(L2)/S(L1) = (L2/L1)^2, and with the cube law the weight per unit area (wing loading, or stress W/A) scales as L2/L1.

hypotheses.name: scaling-area-law#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Isometry of the area and of the mass (constant density): named hypotheses, measured to fail within one flying-fish species (Davenport 1992).

hypotheses.name: scaling-area-law#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Nothing about which family is isometric; the theorems bound only families that are.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: If S L = k L^2 for all L > 0 (AreaLaw) then S(L2)/S(L1) = (L2/L1)^2 and log S(L2)/S(L1) = 2 log(L2/L1) (areaLaw_ratio, areaLaw_log).
With CubeLaw W: (W/S)(L2)/(W/S)(L1) = L2/L1, exponent 1 (wingLoading_ratio, wingLoading_log).
assumed: Isometry of the area and of the mass (constant density): named hypotheses, measured to fail within one flying-fish species (Davenport 1992).
Nothing about which family is isometric; the theorems bound only families that are.

C2a.basis: evaluated against one reference specimen (Cypselurus hiraii, Park and Choi 2010 Table 1 model L3); an isometric family is one body plan, so other clades are out of scope
